items.title: TSMC Q3 profit surges to record high on AI demand; says considering Texas fab By Investing.com
items.author: Ambar Warrick
items.highlights: Investing.com-- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, or TSMC, clocked a stronger-than-expected third-quarter profit on Thursday, with earnings hitting another record high on robust demand from the artificial intelligence industry. The company said that it had considered setting up more facilities in the U.S., potentially in Texas, as it races to ramp up capacity and meet increasing demand. The world’s largest contract chipmaker said net profit surged to T$763.06 billion ($23.55 billion) in the three months to September 30. items.title: Can robust TSMC earnings help settle AI jitters? By Investing.com
items.author: Senad Karaahmetovic
items.highlights: Investing.com - TSMC posted a $23.59 billion net profit for the third quarter of 2026, a 68.7% year-over-year surge that marked its sixth consecutive record quarter, yet the earnings beat has done little to arrest a deepening selloff across AI-linked semiconductor stocks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, the world’s largest contract chipmaker and a foundry supplier to NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple, is the stock most exposed to AI hardware demand: its revenue is tied directly to the volume and complexity of chips ordered by hyperscalers and AI accelerator makers.
